reason: Driven on the real master, not read: state=owner-empty, typed '3 October 2026', pressed 'Set the day' (foot correctly shows 'Kept by Orla / Signal Timeline' with no stamp), pressed 'Add a moment'. The resulting owner-flight surface for a project created two seconds ago renders exactly the three claims the finding names: .b-shared = 'Live since 15 July · anyone with the link can read it', the primary bar button = 'Get the link', and the foot = 'Kept by Orla / Updated 15 July 2026'. Pressing that button compounds it: the publish surface reads 'Aisling & Tom have had this since 15 July.' over the demo share token, and the card says 'days away when this was sent'. Four false statements about who is holding a private plan, on the artifact's own first-run path. Not an artefact the reviewer manufactured by stitching two demo frames: the add handler (render-b.js ~1327) deliberately rewrites F.project.name, F.project.primaryDate and F.milestones, and its own comment states 'The plan this opens is genuinely theirs ... not the demonstration plan.' Having taken responsibility for the transition, it drops publication and updatedLabel. The empty state already discriminates on exactly this axis - foot({stamp:false}) because a project that has never held anything has nothing to stamp - and one press later that care is gone. Not already handled: nothing anywhere in fixture.js, render-core.js or render-b.js ever assigns F.publication, so all three unpublished branches ('Only you can see this', 'Publish', 'Send it to X.') are dead in the master; 'Only you can see this' appears zero times in the built page. Not a restatement of a gate: interaction-check.mjs:2559 asserts the verb matches FIXTURE.publication.state, which is a tautology while only one value ever exists - it proves the ternary, never the draft surface. Not out of scope: the DTO shape is untouched, both states already exist in the model, and the fix is two assignments beside the three writes already sitting in that handler - the same kind of fixture write, on the design side of the data-model line. The standing gap is bigger than the stitch: the pre-publish owner surface is the state every real owner occupies from creation until they publish - most of the product's life - and at a 9.5 bar with thirteen graded frames it has never been drawn, shot, audited or asserted, while the most consequential sentence on an owner's screen currently reads as a lie.
sharpenedFix: Take the finding's fix, with two corrections it needs to not regress anything. (1) In the add handler beside the existing writes, set F.publication = { state: 'draft', publishedAt: null } and F.updatedLabel = F.fmt.medium(F.today) + ' 2026'. The three branches then render 'Only you can see this', 'Publish' and today's stamp with no further change. (2) SAID.publish (render-b.js ~1182) is evaluated ONCE at module load via F_PUBLISHED(), so after the fix a draft owner reaching the publish surface would still be announced 'The link is below.' instead of 'Ready to send. The link is below.' Make SAID values functions (or compute the publish strap inside go()) so the live region follows the state rather than the load-time fixture. (3) In the 'copy' handler (render-b.js ~1047), on the first successful clipboard write set F.publication = { state: 'published', publishedAt: F.today } so the verb, the strap and the press heading flip once and together. (4) Add the fourteenth state 'owner-draft' - precedented by owner-undone, which round 7 added for exactly this reason - and add one gate block asserting that on it .b-shared reads 'Only you can see this', the primary verb reads 'Publish', and the foot stamp is today's, so the branch stops being ungraded. Leave the share URL visible in the draft branch: the design's model is publish-on-copy, and the draft heading 'Send it to Aisling & Tom.' already says so correctly.
